# CubeAPM CLI

> Command-line interface for querying distributed traces (Jaeger-compatible), metrics (Prometheus/PromQL), and logs (VictoriaLogs/LogsQL) from a CubeAPM observability server, built to be driven both interactively and programmatically by scripts and coding agents.

`cubeapm` is a single static Go binary that talks to a CubeAPM server's HTTP APIs. It groups its functionality into command groups, `traces`, `metrics`, `logs`, `ingest`, `config`, plus the top-level `login`, `version`, and `update` commands. The `traces`, `metrics`, and `logs` read commands support `table` (default), `json`, and `yaml` output via `-o`/`--output`; JSON is the format intended for scripting and agents. `update --check` also supports `-o json`/`yaml`. `-o` has no effect on `config view` (always YAML), `config get`, `config profiles list`, `version`, `login`, `update` without `--check`, `ingest`, `logs delete run`/`stop`, or `traces dependencies --dot`.

This is an **independent, unofficial** tool. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by CubeAPM or its makers. "CubeAPM" is the name of the third-party product this CLI connects to.

- Binary name: `cubeapm`
- Supported platforms: macOS (darwin), Linux, and Windows; on `amd64` and `arm64` (Windows ships `amd64` only). Released as `.tar.gz` archives (`.zip` on Windows).
- Written in Go (module `github.com/piyush-gambhir/cubeapm-cli/cli-go`).
- The CLI itself stores no telemetry. It sends requests to the CubeAPM server you configure and, only in interactive terminals, checks GitHub for a new release at most once a day (turn that off with `CUBEAPM_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1`).

## Skill (Claude Code / agents)

A ready-made Claude Code skill ships in the repo: https://github.com/piyush-gambhir/cubeapm-cli/blob/main/cubeapm/SKILL.md . Point your agent at that file, or install it as a skill (copy the `cubeapm/` directory, including `references/`, to `~/.claude/skills/cubeapm/`, or load it via your agent's skill mechanism) to teach an agent how to drive `cubeapm`.

## Install

### Install script (macOS / Linux)

Downloads the latest release binary for your OS/arch and installs it (default `/usr/local/bin`).

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/piyush-gambhir/cubeapm-cli/main/install.sh | sh
```

Install a specific version:

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/piyush-gambhir/cubeapm-cli/main/install.sh | VERSION=0.2.7 sh
```

Install to a custom directory (e.g. one already on your `PATH`):

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/piyush-gambhir/cubeapm-cli/main/install.sh | INSTALL_DIR=~/.local/bin sh
```

The script requires `curl` and `tar`. If the install directory is not writable it falls back to `sudo`.

### Build from source (Go 1.26+, Go 1.27.1 recommended)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/piyush-gambhir/cubeapm-cli.git
cd cubeapm-cli/cli-go
make install
```

`make install` installs the binary as `cubeapm` in `go env GOBIN` (or `$(go env GOPATH)/bin` when GOBIN is unset); set `INSTALL_DIR=...` to choose another directory. `make build` instead writes `./cubeapm` inside `cli-go/`.

Other Makefile targets: `make test`, `make lint`, `make fmt`, `make vet`, `make tidy`, `make clean`, `make llms-check`.

### Prebuilt release archives

Download the archive for your platform from the GitHub Releases page and extract the `cubeapm` binary (`cubeapm.exe` on Windows) onto your `PATH`:
https://github.com/piyush-gambhir/cubeapm-cli/releases

### Updating

A release build updates itself in place on macOS, Linux, and Windows:

```bash
cubeapm update --check           # report current and latest versions
cubeapm update --check -o json   # the same, as JSON
cubeapm update                   # ask "Update now? [Y/n]", then install
cubeapm update --yes             # install without asking (required with --no-input)
```

`update` downloads the release archive for your OS and architecture, verifies its SHA-256 checksum against the release's `checksums.txt`, and replaces the binary in place. On Windows the running `cubeapm.exe` is renamed to `cubeapm.exe.old` (deleted on a later run) and the new one takes its place. If the binary's directory is not writable, `update` fails and leaves the current binary untouched: re-run it with `sudo`, or reinstall with the install script into a writable directory (`INSTALL_DIR=~/.local/bin`). In a terminal it asks `Update now? [Y/n]`; under `--no-input`, or without a terminal, it needs `--yes`. A binary that `make install` put in a Go bin directory (`$GOBIN`, `$GOPATH/bin`, or `~/go/bin`) is not replaced: `update` prints `git pull && make install` (run it in your `cubeapm-cli/cli-go` checkout) instead. `update` does not work on a `dev` build. (A `dev` build is one built without version metadata, for example plain `go build`.)

`update --check` always asks GitHub (bypassing the daily cache, which it then refreshes) and exits 0 whether or not an update exists. With `-o json` it prints `current_version`, `latest_version`, `update_available`, `release_url`, and `install_method` (`self` or `go`). Read-only mode blocks `update` but allows `update --check`.

### Update notice

In an interactive terminal, cubeapm checks GitHub for a new release at most once a day, in the background (cached in `update-check.json` in the config directory), and prints a notice on stderr after the command's output, at most once a day per release. On the run that checks, the command waits at most 1 second for GitHub, so a fast command still shows the notice:

```
A new version of cubeapm is available: v<current> -> v<latest>
Update with: cubeapm update
Release notes: https://github.com/piyush-gambhir/cubeapm-cli/releases/tag/v<latest>
```

There is no check, and no network request, when stderr is not a terminal, when `CI` is set, with `--quiet` or `CUBEAPM_QUIET`, when `CUBEAPM_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` or `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` is set, on `dev` builds, or for `update`, `version`, `completion`, and `help`. Scripts, CI jobs, and coding agents therefore never see it. `cubeapm version` also shows the latest known release from that cache, without using the network.

## Authentication

A CubeAPM server may or may not require authentication. The CLI supports exactly two auth methods:

1. **`kratos`**, email + password. CubeAPM fronts its UI/API with Ory Kratos; the CLI performs the full Kratos browser login flow (initiate flow, fetch CSRF token, POST credentials) and receives a session cookie. The cookie (and its expiry) are cached so subsequent invocations reuse it. When a request returns HTTP 401 and credentials are stored, the CLI automatically re-authenticates once and retries, then persists the refreshed cookie back into the active profile.
2. **`none`**, no authentication. For CubeAPM instances exposed without auth (local dev, or networks with their own access control). The CLI connects directly to the API ports.

Auto-detection: if `auth_method` is unset, the CLI picks `kratos` when both email and password are present, otherwise `none`.

### Log in interactively

`cubeapm login` walks through profile name, server address, auth method, and the three ports, tests the connection (using the Prometheus-standard `/api/v1/labels` endpoint), and saves the profile.

```bash
cubeapm login

# Preseed the server (still prompts for everything else)
cubeapm login --server cube.example.com
```

`login` requires an interactive terminal; it fails under `--no-input` (use `cubeapm config set` or environment variables instead).

### Non-interactive auth (CI / agents)

Provide credentials via environment variables or flags and skip `login` entirely:

```bash
export CUBEAPM_SERVER=cube.example.com
export CUBEAPM_EMAIL=user@example.com
export CUBEAPM_PASSWORD=your-password
export CUBEAPM_NO_INPUT=true     # fail instead of prompting if anything is missing

cubeapm traces services -o json
```

Or all on one line (flags beat everything; avoid putting secrets in shell history):

```bash
cubeapm --server cube.example.com --email user@example.com --password secret traces services
```

### Config file

- Path: `~/.config/cubeapm-cli/config.yaml`
- Override the directory with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` → `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cubeapm-cli/config.yaml`
- Created with `0600` permissions (directory `0700`) because it can hold credentials and a session cookie.
- Format: YAML. See "Configuration & profiles" below for the schema.

### Resolution precedence

Connection and output settings are layered in this order (highest wins):

1. **CLI flags** (`--server`, `--email`, `--password`, `--query-port`, `--ingest-port`, `--admin-port`, `--output`, `--profile`)
2. **Environment variables** (`CUBEAPM_*`, see below)
3. **The active profile** in the config file (selected by `--profile`, else `current_profile`)

The safety settings (`--read-only`, `--no-input`, `--quiet`) follow different rules; see "Safety settings" below.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
|----------|--------|
| `CUBEAPM_SERVER` | Server address (hostname, IP, or full URL) |
| `CUBEAPM_EMAIL` | Login email (Kratos auth) |
| `CUBEAPM_PASSWORD` | Login password (Kratos auth) |
| `CUBEAPM_QUERY_PORT` | Query API port (default `3140`) |
| `CUBEAPM_INGEST_PORT` | Ingest API port (default `3130`) |
| `CUBEAPM_ADMIN_PORT` | Admin API port (default `3199`) |
| `CUBEAPM_READ_ONLY` | Turns read-only mode on when set to a true Go boolean (`true`, `1`, ...); `false`/`0` never turns off a profile's `read_only: true` |
| `CUBEAPM_NO_INPUT` | Disable all interactive prompts when exactly `true` or `1` |
| `CUBEAPM_QUIET` | Suppress informational output when exactly `true` or `1` (ignored if `--quiet` is passed); also turns off the update notice |
| `CUBEAPM_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER`, `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER` | Any non-empty value turns off the update notice and its GitHub release check |
| `CI` | Any non-empty value turns off the update notice and its GitHub release check |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | Relocate the config directory |

There is no environment variable for output format or profile selection, use `-o`/`--output` and `--profile` (or set `output` in the profile via `cubeapm config set output ...`).

## Global flags

These persistent flags apply to every command:

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
|------|-------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--output` | `-o` | string | `table` | Output format: `table`, `json`, or `yaml` |
| `--profile` | | string | | Connection profile to use (overrides `current_profile`) |
| `--server` | | string | | CubeAPM server address override |
| `--email` | | string | | Login email override |
| `--password` | | string | | Login password override |
| `--query-port` | | int | `3140` | Query API port override |
| `--ingest-port` | | int | `3130` | Ingest API port override |
| `--admin-port` | | int | `3199` | Admin API port override |
| `--no-color` | | bool | `false` | Disable colored/bold output |
| `--verbose` | | bool | `false` | Log the full HTTP request/response cycle (auth headers redacted) |
| `--read-only` | | bool | `false` | Block every write command (safety mode for agents); `--read-only=false` cannot turn it off |
| `--no-input` | | bool | `false` | Disable all interactive prompts (CI/agent use) |
| `--quiet` | `-q` | bool | `false` | Suppress informational (non-data) output |

### Ports

CubeAPM exposes three ports. Most commands only use the query port.

| Port | Default | Used by |
|------|---------|---------|
| Query | `3140` | all `traces`, `metrics`, and `logs` read commands |
| Ingest | `3130` | `ingest metrics`, `ingest logs` |
| Admin | `3199` | `logs delete run`, `logs delete list`, `logs delete stop` |

Behind a reverse proxy on HTTPS, all three are usually the same host on port 443, set all three ports to the same value (e.g. `443`) or pass the server as a full `https://` URL.

### Time-range flags

These commands accept `--from`, `--to`, and `--last`: `traces search`, `get`, `services` (only with `--env`), `dependencies`, `callers` (only the end time is used; the rate window is `--window`); `metrics query-range`, `labels`, `label-values`, `series`; `logs query`, `hits`, `stats`, `streams`, `field-names`, `field-values`. `logs status` uses `--lookback <days>` instead, and the remaining commands take no time flags. If none are given, the default window is the **last 1 hour**.

- `--last <dur>`, relative duration from now: `30m`, `1h`, `2d`, `1d12h`, `90s`. Units: `ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d` (note: Go's stdlib lacks `d`, so this CLI adds it). When set, `--last` takes precedence over `--from`/`--to`.
- `--from`/`--to`, accept RFC3339 (`2024-01-15T10:00:00Z`), date-only (`2024-01-15`), date+time without a zone (`2024-01-15T10:00:00`, interpreted as **local** time), Unix seconds (`1705312800`) or milliseconds (`>= 1e12`), or relative (`-1h`, `now-30m`, `now`).
- Only `--from` → `--to` defaults to now. Only `--to` → `--from` defaults to one hour before `--to`.

The `metrics query` command uses a single `--time` flag (same accepted formats) for the instant evaluation timestamp instead of a range.

### Safety settings

- **Read-only:** only ever added, never removed. It is on when the profile has `read_only: true`, when `CUBEAPM_READ_ONLY` is a true Go boolean (`true`, `1`, ...), or when `--read-only` is passed. `CUBEAPM_READ_ONLY=false` and `--read-only=false` cannot turn off a profile's `read_only: true`. When on, every write command is blocked with an error: `ingest metrics`, `ingest logs`, `logs delete run`, `logs delete stop`, `config set`, `config profiles use`, `config profiles delete`, and `update` (`update --check` still runs). All queries, `logs delete list`, `config view`, `config get`, `config profiles list`, and `version` still run. `login` is not covered; it is interactive, so `--no-input` blocks it. For the `config` write commands and `update`, the active profile's `read_only` applies even when `--profile` names another profile, because they change the active profile (or the binary).
- **No-input:** on if `--no-input` is passed or `CUBEAPM_NO_INPUT` is `1`/`true`; `--no-input=false` does not override the environment. `login` fails instead of prompting, and `update` installs only with `--yes`.
- **Quiet:** `--quiet` wins when passed (including `--quiet=false`); otherwise `CUBEAPM_QUIET` (`1`/`true`) applies.

## Commands

Top-level commands: `traces`, `metrics`, `logs`, `ingest`, `config`, `login`, `version`, `update`. Built-in `help` and `completion` are provided by the CLI framework. Group aliases: `traces`→`trace`, `metrics`→`metric`, `logs`→`log`.

PromQL and LogsQL expressions are passed as **positional arguments**, not flags. Always wrap them in single quotes to protect `{`, `}`, `(`, `)`, `|`, and `*` from the shell.

---

### traces, distributed traces (Jaeger-compatible API)

Search, retrieve, and analyze spans. Group alias: `trace`. Uses the query port.

#### traces search

```
cubeapm traces search [flags]
```

Search for traces matching filters. Table output shows the root span per matching trace: `TRACE_ID`, `SERVICE`, `OPERATION`, `DURATION`, `STATUS`, `TIMESTAMP`.

**Required on many CubeAPM deployments:** both `--service` and `--env` must be provided. The server returns a clear error if either is missing. Environment values are UPPER-CASE (e.g. `PROD`, `UAT`).

Flags:
- `--service <name>`, filter by service name (e.g. `api-gateway`)
- `--env <env>`, filter by environment (UPPER-CASE values: `PROD`, `UAT`, etc.)
- `--query <op>`, filter by operation name (e.g. `GET /api/users`)
- `--status <error|ok>`, `error` matches the `error=true` tag; `ok` matches `otel.status_code=OK`
- `--min-duration <dur>`, only traces slower than this (`500ms`, `1s`, `100us`)
- `--max-duration <dur>`, only traces faster than this (`5s`, `10s`)
- `--tags <key=value>`, span tag filter, repeatable (e.g. `--tags http.method=POST --tags http.status_code=500`)
- `--span-kind <kind>`, `client`, `server`, `producer`, `consumer`, `internal`. **Default `server`** (some CubeAPM deployments require a non-empty value).
- `--index <name>`, CubeAPM trace index to query (default `cube:latency`; also `cube:error`)
- `--limit <n>`, max traces to return (default `20`)
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
# Errors slower than 500ms for a service in the last hour
cubeapm traces search --service payments --env PROD --status error --min-duration 500ms --last 1h

# Filter by operation and tags, output JSON, extract trace IDs
cubeapm traces search --service api-gateway --env PROD --query "GET /api/users" \
  --tags http.status_code=500 -o json | jq -r '.[].TRACE_ID'
```

#### traces get

```
cubeapm traces get <trace-id> [flags]
```

Retrieve one trace by its (hex) trace ID. In table mode renders a span waterfall tree (service / operation / duration / status, with parent-child indentation). In JSON/YAML returns the full Jaeger-format trace (all spans, tags, logs, processes).

Flags: `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, optional, narrows the lookup window.

```bash
cubeapm traces get abc123def456789
cubeapm traces get abc123def456789 -o json
```

#### traces services

```
cubeapm traces services [flags]
```

List all services that have reported traces (sorted). Alias: `svc`. Column: `SERVICE`.

With `--env`, list only services visible in a specific environment (e.g. `PROD`, `UAT`). This path is metrics-derived: it queries label-values filtered by `env` and `cube.environment` labels, then unions `service` and `service.name` label values. A service that emits only traces (no metrics) in that environment may not appear.

Flags:
- `--env <env>`, list only services seen in this environment (metrics-derived; UPPER-CASE values)
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range for the metrics lookup (default last 1h; only used with `--env`)

```bash
cubeapm traces services
cubeapm traces svc -o json

# List services active in PROD (env values are UPPER-CASE)
cubeapm traces services --env PROD
cubeapm traces services --env PROD --last 24h -o json
```

#### traces operations

```
cubeapm traces operations <service> [flags]
```

List operations (endpoints/methods) reported by a service. Alias: `ops`. Columns: `OPERATION`, `SPAN_KIND`.

**Caveat:** this endpoint is not exposed by all CubeAPM deployments. When not exposed, the server returns a "unsupported path requested" error. The CLI surfaces this as a clear message: run `cubeapm traces search --service <svc> --env <ENV>` and read the OPERATION column instead.

Flags: `--span-kind <kind>`, filter by span kind (no default; empty = all kinds).

```bash
cubeapm traces operations api-gateway
cubeapm traces ops api-gateway --span-kind server -o json
```

#### traces dependencies

```
cubeapm traces dependencies [flags]
```

Service dependency graph over a time range. Alias: `deps`. Columns: `PARENT`, `CHILD`, `CALL_COUNT`.

**Caveat:** this endpoint is not exposed by all CubeAPM deployments. When not exposed, the server returns a "unsupported path requested" error and the CLI surfaces it as a clear message.

Flags:
- `--dot`, emit Graphviz DOT instead of a table (pipe to `dot`)
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm traces dependencies --last 24h
cubeapm traces deps --last 24h --dot | dot -Tpng -o deps.png
```

#### traces callers

```
cubeapm traces callers [flags]
```

Rank the services making outbound HTTP calls to a host (or reaching a target service), by call rate. This is a convenience wrapper over the PromQL query `topk(N, sum by (service) (rate(cube_apm_latency_count{group_name="HTTP <host>",span_kind="client"}[<window>])))`. Columns: `CALLER_SERVICE`, `CALLS_PER_SEC`.

Flags:
- `--host <host>`, target host, matched against the `group_name` label (e.g. `api.spyne.ai`). Either `--host` or `--service` is required.
- `--service <name>`, keep only client spans whose `span_name` contains this service name. Without `--host`, the host is not inferred: it defaults to the hardcoded `api.spyne.ai`, so pass `--host` for any other deployment
- `--window <dur>`, rate window (default `2m`; shorter = more responsive but noisier)
- `--topk <n>`, max callers to return (default `10`)
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, the query evaluates once at the end of the range (`--to`, else now), so the rate covers only `--window` before that point; `--from` and the length of `--last` have no effect

```bash
# Who's calling api.spyne.ai right now?
cubeapm traces callers --host api.spyne.ai --last 1h

# Biggest callers at the end of an incident window, top 20, 5m rate window
cubeapm traces callers --host api.spyne.ai --window 5m --topk 20 \
  --to 2026-04-19T13:50:00Z
```

---

### metrics, Prometheus-compatible metrics (PromQL)

Run PromQL and explore label/series metadata. Group alias: `metric`. Uses the query port.

#### metrics query

```
cubeapm metrics query <promql> [flags]
```

Instant PromQL query at a single point in time. Table columns for a vector result: `METRIC`, `VALUE`, `TIMESTAMP` (scalar/string results print the value). JSON/YAML returns the raw Prometheus API response.

Flags: `--time <t>`, evaluation timestamp (RFC3339, Unix, or relative like `now-1h`; default now).

```bash
cubeapm metrics query 'up'
cubeapm metrics query 'sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total[5m]))'
cubeapm metrics query 'histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(http_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))' --time now-1h
```

#### metrics query-range

```
cubeapm metrics query-range <promql> [flags]
```

Range PromQL query over a window. Alias: `range`. Table columns: `METRIC`, `SAMPLES`, `VALUES` (a sampled summary). JSON/YAML returns the full matrix.

Flags:
- `--step <dur>`, resolution between data points (`15s`, `1m`, `5m`, `1h`). If omitted, auto-calculated to ~250 points.
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm metrics query-range 'rate(http_requests_total[5m])' --last 1h --step 1m
cubeapm metrics query-range 'sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total[5m]))' --last 6h --step 5m -o json
```

#### metrics labels

```
cubeapm metrics labels [flags]
```

List all metric label names (sorted). Column: `LABEL`. Flags: `--from` / `--to` / `--last` (default last 1h).

```bash
cubeapm metrics labels --last 24h
```

#### metrics label-values

```
cubeapm metrics label-values <label> [flags]
```

List all values for a given label (sorted). Column: `VALUE`.

Flags:
- `--like <substr>`, case-insensitive substring filter on returned values
- `--match <selector>`, series selector to scope returned values; repeatable and ORed (e.g. `--match '{env="PROD"}'`). Uses the Prometheus `match[]` extension. Useful to avoid the 30k-cardinality limit that applies to the unfiltered endpoint.
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm metrics label-values __name__
cubeapm metrics label-values service --like media --last 24h

# List service names only in the PROD environment
cubeapm metrics label-values service.name --match '{env="PROD"}'

# Scope with cube.environment label (some CubeAPM metrics use this instead of env)
cubeapm metrics label-values service.name --match '{cube.environment="PROD"}'
```

#### metrics series

```
cubeapm metrics series [flags]
```

Find time series matching one or more selectors. At least one `--match` is required. Column: `SERIES` (rendered as `metric{label="value", ...}`).

Flags:
- `--match <selector>`, series selector in PromQL label-matching syntax, repeatable (e.g. `up{job="api"}`, `{__name__=~"http_.*"}`)
- `--limit <n>`, max series (default `0` = unlimited)
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm metrics series --match 'http_requests_total' --match 'process_cpu_seconds_total'
cubeapm metrics series --match '{__name__=~"http_.*"}' --last 24h --limit 50 -o json
```

---

### logs, logs (VictoriaLogs-compatible, LogsQL)

Query logs with LogsQL, explore fields/streams, probe retention, and manage deletions. Group alias: `log`. Read commands use the query port; `logs delete *` uses the admin port.

LogsQL quick reference: `*` (all), `error` (keyword), `service:api` (field), `error AND service:api`, `error OR warn`, `NOT health_check`, `_stream:{host="web-1"}`, `re("pattern")`, `_time:1h`, `status:>400`, and `... | stats <fn> by (<fields>)` pipelines.

#### logs query

```
cubeapm logs query <logsql> [flags]
```

Run a LogsQL query and return matching entries. Table columns: `TIMESTAMP`, `STREAM`, `MESSAGE` (truncated). In JSON/YAML, entries are streamed one object at a time, not as an array: `-o json` emits a sequence of pretty-printed JSON objects (`jq` reads it as a stream), and `-o yaml` emits one YAML document per entry separated by `---`. Each entry has `_time`, `_stream`, `_msg`, and non-underscore fields.

The `--service`, `--level`, and `--stream` flags are convenience prefixes AND-joined in front of your query (`--service api` → `service:api AND (<your query>)`).

Flags:
- `--service <name>`, prepend `service:<value>`
- `--level <level>`, prepend `level:<value>` (`error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`)
- `--stream <sel>`, prepend `_stream:<value>` (e.g. `{host="web-1"}`)
- `--limit <n>`, max entries (default `100`)
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm logs query 'error' --service api-gateway --last 30m
cubeapm logs query 'error AND service:api AND NOT health_check' --last 30m
cubeapm logs query 'error' -o json | jq '.["_msg"]'
```

#### logs hits

```
cubeapm logs hits [flags]
```

Log-volume histogram (counts per time bucket) for a query. Columns: `TIMESTAMP`, `COUNT`.

Flags:
- `--query <logsql>`, query to count (default `*`)
- `--step <dur>`, bucket size (`5m`, `1h`); if omitted, the CLI uses the range divided by 60 (minimum `1s`)
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm logs hits --query 'error' --last 24h --step 1h
cubeapm logs hits --query 'service:api-gateway' --last 6h --step 15m -o json
```

#### logs status

```
cubeapm logs status [flags]
```

Probe effective log retention (CubeAPM does not expose it directly). Samples 24h buckets over the lookback window and reports the oldest/newest non-empty buckets, approximate retention hours, and a note when retention looks shorter than the lookback. JSON fields: `query`, `lookbackDays`, `hasLogs`, `earliestNonZeroBucket`, `latestNonZeroBucket`, `retentionHours`, `nonEmptyDays`, `note`.

Flags:
- `--query <logsql>`, query to probe (default `*`; e.g. `service.name:MEDIA-SERVICE`)
- `--lookback <days>`, lookback window in days (default `30`)

```bash
cubeapm logs status
cubeapm logs status --query 'service.name:MEDIA-SERVICE' --lookback 60 -o json
```

#### logs stats

```
cubeapm logs stats <logsql> [flags]
```

Run a LogsQL stats/aggregation pipeline (the query must contain a `| stats` pipe). Columns are the aggregation's output fields. Stats functions include `count()`, `count_uniq(f)`, `sum(f)`, `avg(f)`, `min(f)`, `max(f)`, `median(f)`, `quantile(0.99, f)`, `values(f)`.

Flags: `--from` / `--to` / `--last` (default last 1h).

```bash
cubeapm logs stats 'error | stats by (service) count() as c' --last 24h
cubeapm logs stats '* | stats count_uniq(user_id) by (service)' --last 1h -o json
```

#### logs streams

```
cubeapm logs streams [flags]
```

List log streams (unique stream-label sets) and their entry counts. Columns: `STREAM`, `ENTRIES`.

Flags:
- `--query <logsql>`, filter which streams to include
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm logs streams --last 1h
cubeapm logs streams --query 'service:api-gateway' --last 1h -o json
```

#### logs field-names

```
cubeapm logs field-names [flags]
```

Discover available log field names and their hit counts. Alias: `fields`. Columns: `FIELD`, `HITS`.

Flags:
- `--query <logsql>`, restrict to entries matching this query
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm logs field-names --last 1h
cubeapm logs fields --query 'level:error' --last 1h -o json
```

#### logs field-values

```
cubeapm logs field-values <field> [flags]
```

List values for a specific log field and their hit counts. Columns: `VALUE`, `HITS`.

Flags:
- `--query <logsql>`, restrict to entries matching this query
- `--limit <n>`, max values (default `100`)
- `--from` / `--to` / `--last`, time range (default last 1h)

```bash
cubeapm logs field-values status --last 1h
cubeapm logs field-values host --query 'error' --limit 50 -o json
```

#### logs delete

```
cubeapm logs delete <run|stop|list>
```

Manage asynchronous log-deletion tasks via the admin API (port 3199). `run` and `stop` are **mutating** and blocked under read-only mode; `list` is read-only and always allowed.

##### logs delete run

```
cubeapm logs delete run <filter>
```

Start a deletion task with a LogsQL filter. Deletion is **irreversible**, preview with `cubeapm logs query <same filter>` first. Returns a task ID.

```bash
cubeapm logs delete run '_time:<24h AND service:test'
cubeapm logs delete run '_stream:{env="staging"}'
```

##### logs delete list

```
cubeapm logs delete list
```

List active deletion tasks. Alias: `ls`. Columns: `TASK_ID`, `FILTER`, `STATUS`, `PROGRESS`.

```bash
cubeapm logs delete list -o json
```

##### logs delete stop

```
cubeapm logs delete stop <task-id> [flags]
```

Stop a running deletion task. Already-deleted entries are not restored.

Flags: `--if-exists`, succeed silently if the task does not exist (idempotent).

```bash
cubeapm logs delete stop abc123-def456
cubeapm logs delete stop --if-exists abc123-def456
```

---

### ingest, push data to CubeAPM (ingest API, port 3130)

Push metrics or logs read from a file or stdin. Both subcommands are **mutating** (blocked under read-only mode).

#### ingest metrics

```
cubeapm ingest metrics [flags]
```

Push metrics. Formats: `prometheus` (exposition/text, default), `otlp` (OpenTelemetry protobuf binary), `remote-write` (Prometheus remote write, Snappy-compressed protobuf).

Ingest endpoints (on `http://<server>:<ingest-port>`, default port 3130):
- `prometheus`: POST /api/metrics/v1/save
- `otlp`: POST /api/metrics/v1/save/otlp
- `remote-write`: POST /api/metrics/api/v1/write

Flags:
- `--format <fmt>`, `prometheus` | `otlp` | `remote-write` (default `prometheus`)
- `--file <path>`, input file; `-` for stdin (default `-`). With no `--file`, stdin must be piped/redirected.

```bash
cubeapm ingest metrics --format prometheus --file metrics.txt
curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | cubeapm ingest metrics --format prometheus
cubeapm ingest metrics --format otlp --file metrics.pb
cubeapm ingest metrics --format remote-write --file remote-write.pb
```

#### ingest logs

```
cubeapm ingest logs [flags]
```

Push logs. Formats: `jsonline` (newline-delimited JSON, default), `otlp` (protobuf), `loki` (Loki push JSON), `elastic` (Elasticsearch bulk NDJSON).

Ingest endpoints (on `http://<server>:<ingest-port>`, default port 3130):
- `jsonline`: POST /api/logs/insert/jsonline
- `otlp`: POST /api/logs/insert/opentelemetry/v1/logs
- `loki`: POST /api/logs/insert/loki/api/v1/push
- `elastic`: POST /api/logs/insert/elasticsearch/_bulk

Flags:
- `--format <fmt>`, `jsonline` | `otlp` | `loki` | `elastic` (default `jsonline`)
- `--file <path>`, input file; `-` for stdin (default `-`)

```bash
cubeapm ingest logs --format jsonline --file logs.jsonl
cat logs.jsonl | cubeapm ingest logs --format jsonline
cubeapm ingest logs --format loki --file loki-push.json
cubeapm ingest logs --format elastic --file elastic-bulk.ndjson
```

A jsonline record looks like: `{"_time":"2024-01-15T10:00:00Z","_msg":"request completed","service":"api"}`.

---

### config, configuration & profiles

```
cubeapm config <view|set|get|profiles>
```

View and edit configuration and connection profiles. These commands do not contact the server.

#### config view

```
cubeapm config view
```

Print the config file path and its full contents as YAML, with `password` and `session_cookie` masked.

#### config set

```
cubeapm config set <key> <value>
```

Set a value in the current profile (creating a `default` profile if none is active) and save. Blocked in read-only mode. Valid keys: `server`, `email`, `password`, `auth_method` (`kratos`|`none`), `query_port`, `ingest_port`, `admin_port`, `output` (`table`|`json`|`yaml`).

```bash
cubeapm config set server cube.example.com
cubeapm config set output json
cubeapm config set auth_method kratos
```

#### config get

```
cubeapm config get <key>
```

Read a value from the resolved current profile (with defaults applied). `password` is masked. Valid keys: `server`, `email`, `password`, `auth_method`, `query_port`, `ingest_port`, `admin_port`, `output`, `current_profile`.

```bash
cubeapm config get server
cubeapm config get current_profile
```

#### config profiles

```
cubeapm config profiles <list|use|delete>
```

- `config profiles list` (alias `ls`), list all profiles; the active one is marked `*`.
- `config profiles use <name>`, set the active profile.
- `config profiles delete <name>` (alias `rm`), delete a profile; clears `current_profile` if it was active.

`use` and `delete` are blocked in read-only mode.

```bash
cubeapm config profiles list
cubeapm config profiles use production
cubeapm config profiles delete staging
```

---

### login

```
cubeapm login [--server <addr>]
```

Interactively create/update a connection profile: prompts for profile name (default `default`), server, auth method (1 = Email/Password, 2 = No authentication), and the three ports; tests the connection; saves the profile (and makes it active if none was). Requires an interactive terminal, fails under `--no-input`.

### version

```
cubeapm version
```

Print the CLI version, commit hash, and build date. (A build without version metadata, for example plain `go build`, reports `dev`.) When an earlier command already checked for releases, it also prints `latest:` and `update_available:` from the local cache; it never uses the network.

### update

```
cubeapm update [--check] [--yes|-y]
```

Check for and install the latest release on macOS, Linux, or Windows. `--check` only reports (current and latest version, whether an update is available, the release notes URL; `-o json` gives `current_version`, `latest_version`, `update_available`, `release_url`, `install_method`) and exits 0 either way. Without `--check`, it prints `v<current> -> v<latest>`, asks `Update now? [Y/n]` in a terminal (`--yes` skips the question; with `--no-input` or without a terminal it fails unless `--yes` is given), verifies the archive's SHA-256 checksum, replaces the binary (Windows: the old one is renamed to `cubeapm.exe.old`), and prints `Updated cubeapm v<current> -> v<latest>`. An unwritable install directory fails with advice (sudo, or reinstall into a writable directory) and leaves the old binary working. A binary in a Go bin directory is not replaced; it prints `git pull && make install` instead. Fails on a `dev` build. Read-only mode blocks `update` but allows `update --check`.

## Output formats

Select with `-o`/`--output`. Default is `table`.

- **table**, aligned, bold-headed columns for humans (color/bold disabled by `--no-color`).
- **json**, pretty-printed JSON. Table-style results become a JSON array of objects keyed by the column headers (e.g. `SERVICE`, `TRACE_ID`); raw API responses (e.g. `metrics query`) are returned verbatim. HTML escaping is disabled so query strings stay readable. **This is the format for scripting and agents.**
- **yaml**, the same data as YAML.

Errors are written to stderr; under `-o json` they are emitted as a structured object `{"error": "...", "status_code": <n>}`.

```bash
cubeapm traces services                  # table
cubeapm traces services -o json          # JSON array of {"SERVICE": "..."}
cubeapm metrics query 'up' -o yaml        # YAML
```

Set a persistent default in the active profile:

```bash
cubeapm config set output json
```

## Configuration & profiles

The config file lives at `~/.config/cubeapm-cli/config.yaml` (or under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). It holds named **profiles** plus the `current_profile` pointer. Pick a profile per-command with `--profile`, or switch the default with `cubeapm config profiles use`.

Schema (fields are omitted when empty/default):

```yaml
current_profile: production
profiles:
  production:
    server: cube.example.com        # hostname, IP, or full http(s):// URL
    auth_method: kratos             # "kratos" or "none" (empty = auto-detect)
    email: admin@example.com        # for kratos auth
    password: your-password         # stored to enable silent re-auth
    session_cookie: "ory_kratos_session=..."  # cached after login (masked in `config view`)
    session_expiry: "2024-01-16T18:00:00Z"     # RFC3339
    query_port: 3140
    ingest_port: 3130
    admin_port: 3199
    output: table                   # default output format for this profile
    read_only: false                # block writes when true
  local:
    server: localhost
    auth_method: none
```

Notes:
- Profiles are created by `cubeapm login` or by `cubeapm config set` (which seeds a `default` profile if none exists).
- The session cookie and its expiry are written automatically after a successful Kratos login and refreshed on auto-re-auth.
- The file is saved with `0600` permissions. Prefer environment variables over storing `password` in the file for higher-security setups.

## Environments

CubeAPM uses an environment label to segment telemetry by deployment stage (production, UAT, etc.).

Key facts:
- Environment values are UPPER-CASE: `PROD`, `UAT`, `STAGING`, etc.
- The label name is inconsistent across metric families: some use `env`, others use `cube.environment`. `traces services --env` queries both automatically. `metrics label-values --match` sends your selector unchanged, so you choose the label name; to cover both, run it once with `{env="PROD"}` and once with `{cube.environment="PROD"}`.
- `traces search` requires both `--service` and `--env` on most CubeAPM deployments (the server returns a clear error if either is missing).
- `traces operations` and `traces dependencies` are not exposed by all CubeAPM deployments. When unavailable, the server returns an "unsupported path" error. Use `traces search` and read the OPERATION column to discover operations instead.
- To list services in an environment, use `cubeapm traces services --env PROD` (metrics-derived, may miss trace-only services) or `cubeapm metrics label-values service.name --match '{env="PROD"}'` (avoids the 30k-cardinality series limit).

## Examples / recipes

### Fully non-interactive setup (CI / agent)

```bash
export CUBEAPM_SERVER=cube.example.com
export CUBEAPM_EMAIL="$CUBEAPM_EMAIL"
export CUBEAPM_PASSWORD="$CUBEAPM_PASSWORD"
export CUBEAPM_NO_INPUT=true       # fail instead of prompting
export CUBEAPM_READ_ONLY=true      # belt-and-suspenders: block accidental writes

cubeapm traces services -o json
cubeapm metrics query 'up' -o json
```

### Investigate a production error end-to-end

```bash
# 1. Recent error traces for a service
cubeapm traces search --service payments --status error --last 1h -o json

# 2. Inspect one trace's span waterfall
cubeapm traces get <trace-id> -o json

# 3. Correlated error logs in the same window
cubeapm logs query 'level:error AND service:payments' --last 1h -o json

# 4. Error-rate metric
cubeapm metrics query 'rate(http_requests_total{service="payments",status=~"5.."}[5m])' -o json
```

### Find who suddenly started calling a host

```bash
cubeapm traces callers --host api.spyne.ai --last 1h --window 5m --topk 20 -o json
```

### Explore log schema before querying

```bash
cubeapm logs field-names --last 1h -o json
cubeapm logs field-values service --last 1h -o json
cubeapm logs streams --last 1h -o json
```

### Confirm logs still exist for an old incident window

```bash
cubeapm logs status --query 'service.name:MEDIA-SERVICE' --lookback 60 -o json | jq '.retentionHours, .earliestNonZeroBucket'
```

### Extract structured fields with jq

```bash
# Trace IDs and durations
cubeapm traces search --service api-gateway --last 1h -o json | jq '.[] | {TRACE_ID, DURATION, OPERATION}'

# Service list
cubeapm traces services -o json | jq -r '.[].SERVICE'

# Metric values
cubeapm metrics query 'up' -o json | jq '.data.result[] | {instance: .metric.instance, value: .value[1]}'

# Error counts per service from a stats query
cubeapm logs stats 'level:error | stats by (service) count() as c' --last 1h -o json | jq '.'
```

### Ingest metrics scraped from a Prometheus exporter

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | cubeapm ingest metrics --format prometheus
```

### List services active in a specific environment

```bash
# Via traces services (metrics-derived; may miss trace-only services)
cubeapm traces services --env PROD
cubeapm traces services --env UAT --last 24h -o json

# Via metrics label-values with a series selector (avoids the 30k-cardinality limit)
cubeapm metrics label-values service.name --match '{env="PROD"}'
cubeapm metrics label-values service.name --match '{cube.environment="PROD"}'

# Both labels at once: run both commands and union the results
cubeapm metrics label-values service.name --match '{env="PROD"}' -o json
cubeapm metrics label-values service.name --match '{cube.environment="PROD"}' -o json
```

### Search traces in an environment (both flags typically required)

```bash
# On most CubeAPM deployments, both --service and --env are required for traces search
cubeapm traces search --service payments --env PROD --last 1h -o json

# Find operations when traces operations is not exposed
cubeapm traces search --service payments --env PROD --last 1h -o json | jq -r '.[].OPERATION' | sort -u
```

### Render the service dependency graph

```bash
cubeapm traces dependencies --last 24h --dot | dot -Tpng -o deps.png
```

### Switch between instances

```bash
cubeapm --profile staging traces services        # one-off
cubeapm config profiles use production            # change the default
```
